Regulation: B.C. Reg. 150/2026
Made under: Employment Standards Act
Published in: No. 15 – B.C. Regs. 149 to 152, August 25, including August 11, 2026
Deposit date: August 6, 2026

B.C. Reg. 150/2026, deposited August 6, 2026, under theEMPLOYMENT STANDARDS ACT[section 127 (2)]. Order in Council 373/2026, approved and ordered August 6, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that the Reservists’ Leave Regulation, B.C. Reg. 254/2016, is amended as set out in the attached Schedule. — J. WHITESIDE,Minister of Labour; J. OSBORNE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Section 2 of the Reservists’ Leave Regulation, B.C. Reg. 254/2016, is amended (a)	in subsection (1) by striking out "Canadian Forces training activities" and substituting "military skills training activities", (b)	by repealing subsection (2) and substituting the following: (2)	For the purposes of section 52.2 (3) of the Act, the maximum combined total of all leave taken for the purpose described in section 52 (2) (a) of the Act and all leave taken in the circumstance prescribed under subsection (1) of this section is 24 months in any period of 60 months., and (c)	in subsection (3) by adding "of the Act" after "section 52.2 (4) (b) (iii)". minutes_briefs.title: BC expands reservists' leave rules and caps combined military leave at 24 months
minutes_briefs.summary: BC has changed the Reservists' Leave Regulation under the Employment Standards Act. The leave now covers 'military skills training activities' instead of only 'Canadian Forces training activities', which means more kinds of military training may qualify. The regulation also sets a new maximum: an employee can take no more than 24 months of combined leave in any 60-month period, counting both the general leave for military service and this reservists' training leave.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Update your leave policy and records so reservists' training leave uses the new wording and the 24-month cap in any 60 months is tracked.
